steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square pan.

Blend sugar, melted butter, and vanilla in a large bowl. Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Gradually mix into egg mixture until combined. Spread into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until brownies begin pulling away from the sides of the pan, 40 to 45 minutes. Let brownies cool, then cut into squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Deep-Dish Brownies
raw_recipe.description: These thick 8x8-inch pan brownies are made with butter, sugar, vanilla, eggs, and lots of rich cocoa powder for a decadent deep-dish chocolate treat.
raw_recipe.name: Deep-Dish Brownies

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square pan.

Blend sugar, melted butter, and vanilla in a large bowl. Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Gradually mix into egg mixture until combined. Spread into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until brownies begin pulling away from the sides of the pan, 40 to 45 minutes. Let brownies cool, then cut into squares.

review.reviewBody: Great chewy, fudgy brownie IF you eliminate one egg, and add more cocoa (1/4 cup). No baking powder, or else it will rise too much like a cake. Not really deep dish, but just regular size thickness. And make it easy on yourself folks, this can be a one-bowl recipe. I just add all the dry ingredients into the wet mixture and slowly stir until it's all incorporated. Definitely increase cocoa and add 3 tablespoons sugar to compensate. I also used just 1/2 stick of butter and 1/4 cup applesauce and it was super moist and hopefully a smidge healthier. This is a really easy recipe and quick and fun to do with kids. Why use stuff from a box with all those preservatives when this is soooo easy. Bake no longer than 35 min in 8x8 square pan. Tip for all brownie recipes: grease only the bottom of your pan, not the sides to avoid burning or turning too crisp or dark on the sides of the brownies. With a few changes, this one is my master recipe.

I was pleased with these deep, dark, chocolatey, moist, fudgy brownies. Just for something fun and different I added quartered Oreos to the batter. When the brownies were nearly done I topped them with more crumbled Oreos and miniature marshmallows and popped them under the broiler for a minute or two until the marshmallows were melted and a light golden brown. To gild the lily even further I finished them with a drizzle of melted chocolate chips. It takes a good, reliable recipe to mess with it that much!

The chocolate flavor in these is so rich, without being overbearing! Better than any box mix. I followed the recipe as listed, but I did use my KitchenAid paddle attachment for all stages. Doing this, rather than stirring in the dry ingredients by hand, made these brownies more cake-like. I actually prefer cake-like, so I'm really happy!
 
Modification and results: I baked these in a 9 slot silicone pan, giving perfect individual sized brownies. I softened some Dulche de Leche (caramel sauce) and swirled a small amount in each brownie. Because the batter came out cake-like, and with the heaviness of the caramel, just before the brownies were done, they collapsed! They are still very delicious, just not so pretty!)

I will try these again without the Dulche de Leche, and mixing in the dry ingredients by hand, to see the difference. Otherwise, I think these are the best tasting brownies ever and I will make them again!

I used a 9 inch pan and increased the baking powder to 1 tsp (I hadn't read the reviews). I used dutch processed cocoa and I added 1 cup toasted pecans and decreased the baking time to 25 minutes. They came out quite good. I will make them again.

I made this recipe as written, as far as the texture elements were concerned (I did add 2 T finely ground coffee to enhance chocolate). I removed from oven when edges were pulling from the sides of the pan and the center was "just" set and then allowed to cool completely before cutting. I baked in enameled cast iron square. They were a perfect, fudge, thick brownie. Slight crisp on top and pure fudgy goodness below. Pay close attention to the cook and you just can't go wrong. Also, I did not use an electric mixer - just a wooden spoon - so the batter would not be overworked. I'm adding this to my recipe box. No need for another recipe for our family collection!

Hands down the very best brownie recipe!!!! Ok...here is what I did.....FIRST...I doubled the recipe....trust me on this one...you will be glad you did...they are addicting!!! I used real butter....Land O Lakes is the best...but really any real stick butter will do..(don't use margarine)....then I added 4 eggs instead of 6. Then I added an extra 1/2 cup of cocoa to the mix, which would equal 1 1/2 cups of cocoa....OMIT the baking soda AND salt..... and I added 1 cup of chocolate chips (hey..I'm a girlie girl who loves chocolate). I also baked it for 50 minutes......in a 9 X 13 pan. YUM...YUM....YUMMY!!!!! You will want to grab the milk OR top it with some vanilla ice cream!!! A real treat....and TRUST ME....hide it in view or you will be nibbling on this EVERY TIME you walk into your kitchen!!!!!

I made these last night. I doubled the recipe which worked well and used a 9x13 pyrex to bake them in. I had them in for about 43 minutes. I added 1/2 cup milk chocolate chips, 1/2 cup toffee bits, and 1/2 cup chopped walnuts. I also sptinkled the top with nuts and toffee before baking them. My boyfriend brought them to school and he was asked if I ever thought about selling my products! Great recipe! Perfect thickness and texture in a brownie hands down! (with a little help from my imagination of course)

Very quick and easy recipe! But since I always read the reviews, I also omitted the baking powder & added 1/4 cup more of cocoa plus 1/4 cup more of sugar to balance. Also cut eggs down to 2....BUT I DOUBLED the recipe...so I used 4 eggs & went on to dbl each other ingredient. I used the one-bowl method, so I mixed all dry ingredients together first, then added melted butter and vanilla, then added eggs one at a time...I used a Pyrex 13x9 glass dish & only greased the bottom, baked @ 350* for 35 mins. Very moist brownies & they taste out of this world!! Great for chocoholics ;)

I took this recipe to a potluck and everyone loved it. I added 1/2 c of walnuts and also made a basic glaze, sprinkled a few nuts on top. My oven tends to be hot so I cooked it at 325 degrees but it needed extra 10 minutes. A go to recipe for me now! Thanks!

Just made these! Oh my! They're delicious!!! I definitely will not go back to a box mix!!! When they were half way done baking I added semi sweet chocolate chips, cinnamon toast crunch type cereal and mini marshmallows. They are absolutely sinful! Have already been asked when I'm making more!

Added some homemade chocolate sauce (1/2 cup max) drizzled and slowly ribboned through the batter in the pan. Cooked approximately 42.30 minutes. The sauce caramelized a bit where it touched the pan. Took this great recipe to the next level of smack your momma good.
I didn’t make any changes to the recipe. I would definitely not make these again. NOT fudgy and not very tasty either.

I did not change the recipe at all, they were ready in about 40 minutes. I did make a chocolate frosting and spread it on top. My son liked them but thought they were kind of cake-like and prefers a chewier and moist brownie. I personally like these brownies a lot and didn't find them so cake-like.

I found the Deep-Dish Brownie recipe at Hershey's website. So that must be where it is originally from. I like that the recipe on All-Recipes instructs adding the eggs one at a time. That is the proper way to add them. Eeshey'shasyou add them all at once. This is one of my favorite recipe for brownies!

Made no changes but adding some nuts to the batter, and at the last minute added some caramel morsels to the top. They burned a bit, but the brownie recipe was just what I was after. These are definitely not fudge like, and more cake like, which I prefer. Chocolate flavor was still great.
Delicious, chocolatey and chewy. I truly would not change one thing in this recipe.

I made this recipe, sort of, LOL 😂. I added an additional 1/2 cup of sugar 1 additional egg and a 1/4 cup of vegetable oil as well as a 1/2 Cup semi sweet morsels. Now this recipe (which is now mine I suppose) turned out precisely how my wife and kids like it. Chewy, gooey and ready for a few scoops of Costco vanilla ice cream 😋. Will add a photo on the next batch because this one is already gone! I’ll make them agin every Sunday before the football games start as a diversion as I slip out the door to the cigar lounge 😁.
Followed recipe except had to use vegan butter. Not bad, but too pale. All together, too much sugar and not enough cocoa.
Everyone I know has loved these!
